Article Title: Ancient humans in Israel ate snakes and lizards 15,000 years ago; 3,000 bones reveal what was on the menu
Article Text:
3,000 snake and lizard bones found in ancient cave

Ancient snake bones carried repeated marks linked to human handling

Bone damage showed which reptiles were likely eaten by ancient people

Reptiles reveal a wider Natufian diet before farming

At a cave on the slopes of Mount Carmel, thousands of small reptile bones accumulated alongside the remains of animals hunted and gathered by people more than 11,000 years ago. For years, their presence raised a straightforward but difficult question: were the snakes and lizards food, or had they ended up there through the activity of predators?A closer examination of the bones offered an answer. At el-Wad Terrace, archaeologists identified marks and patterns of damage consistent with human handling and consumption. The evidence points to people in the region eating at least some of the reptiles, adding an unexpected detail to what is known about the diet of the Natufian communities who lived there.The study, published in the journal Scientific Reports, titled ‘ Squamate bone taphonomy: A new experimental framework and its application to the Natufian zooarchaeological record ’ examined reptile bones from the 15,000-year-old el-Wad Terrace site in Israel, finding signs of trampling, erosion and breakage but little evidence of digestion.El-Wad Terrace was occupied during the late Pleistocene, with people using the site between roughly 15,000 and 11,500 years ago. Excavations have produced a dense collection of animal remains, including nearly 3,000 bones belonging to snakes and lizards.That is an unusually large share of the assemblage. Squamate remains the group that includes both snakes and lizards accounted for about a third of the animal bones recovered from the site.Most were vertebrae, which makes the archaeological evidence harder to interpret. Unlike the larger bones of deer or other hunted animals, these small pieces can be altered in several ways after an animal dies.Weathering, sediment, fire and the digestive systems of birds of prey can all leave marks on bone.So finding reptile bones near an ancient settlement does not, by itself, prove that people were eating them. The species represented at el-Wad included the European glass lizard, a legless reptile that can grow to a considerable size, as well as large whip snakes, eastern Montpellier snakes and Palestinian vipers. Smaller snakes and lizards were also present.To separate human activity from other possible causes, the researchers carried out experiments using modern squamate bones. They exposed the bones to different processes that could have affected remains at an archaeological site, including weathering, burning, trampling and digestion by birds of prey.The resulting marks provided a set of comparisons for the ancient material. This mattered because the surface of a small reptile vertebra can change substantially after burial, potentially obscuring or resembling traces left during butchery. When the el-Wad bones were examined against those experimental patterns, some of the damage stood out.Several vertebrae from large whip snakes carried cut marks in similar positions. The marks occurred on different bones and, in some cases, appeared on the same side. That repeated pattern was difficult to explain as random damage after burial.The case was strengthened by what was missing from many of the bones. Large whip snake and glass lizard remains generally did not show the digestion damage expected if birds of prey had swallowed the animals and later deposited their bones at the cave.That does not mean every reptile at the site was eaten. The archaeological record was more complicated than that.Some of the smaller snakes and lizards, along with many eastern Montpellier snakes and vipers, appear to have been brought into the cave by raptors or to have arrived through other natural processes. Their presence cannot simply be counted as evidence of human meals.The distinction is important. The study was not suggesting that Natufian people routinely consumed every snake and lizard represented in the excavation. Instead, the bone damage points to particular reptiles, especially large whip snakes and glass lizards having been used as food.The people who occupied el-Wad Terrace belonged to the Natufian culture, which emerged in the Levant towards the end of the Pleistocene. Their communities occupied an interesting point in human history.They were still largely dependent on hunting and gathering, but some groups were living in places for longer periods rather than moving constantly between temporary camps. This semi-sedentary way of life came before the widespread adoption of farming and permanent agricultural settlements.Their diet was varied. People gathered wild plant foods and hunted animals available in the surrounding landscape. The reptile remains suggest that smaller, less conventional sources of meat could also find their way onto the menu.Snakes and lizards would not necessarily have provided the same quantity of meat as larger game, but their remains show that the range of food being used by these communities was broader than the most obvious archaeological discoveries might suggest.
Article Summary: 3,000 snake and lizard bones found in ancient cave in Israel. Bones carried repeated marks linked to human handling. Bone damage showed which reptiles were likely eaten by ancient people. Reptiles reveal a wider Natufian diet before farming.

Article Title: Imran Khan’s sister meets him after 9 months as Pakistan SC orders hospital transfer for jailed ex-PM
Article Text:
Former Pak PM is set to be shifted to a hospital after top court's order over health concerns

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan ’s sister Noreen Niazi met him at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail on Tuesday after a gap of around nine months, following a Supreme Court order allowing weekly meetings between the former prime minister and his family amid concerns over his health.The meeting lasted around 15 minutes, according to jail sources, cited by Express Tribune. Noreen briefed Imran on the Supreme Court’s order regarding his transfer to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital and enquired about his health. The two also discussed ongoing legal matters.Noreen confirmed after the meeting that she had met her brother but did not speak to the media, in line with an assurance given before the court. She later left Adiala Jail with her sisters Aleema Khan and Uzma Khan.Imran also met his wife, Bushra Bibi, with their meeting lasting around 30-35 minutes. Bushra earlier met her daughter, Mubashra Sheikh, and sister-in-law Mehrunnisa.Before entering the jail, Noreen told reporters that she would inform Imran that “the Supreme Court has granted you permission” to meet his family. She also said she would brief him about efforts made by PTI workers on his behalf.The meetings followed a three-member Supreme Court bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed directing the government to facilitate weekly meetings between Imran and his family. The court was hearing petitions concerning his access to his sisters and personal physicians, as well as his medical condition.The order came after a medical board report and a report by the Adiala Jail superintendent were submitted to the court. The reports recommended more frequent meetings with Imran’s immediate family and spouse to help manage his blood pressure and anxiety.The Supreme Court also ordered that Imran be moved to Shifa International Hospital for treatment and directed the formation of a medical board comprising an eye specialist, general physician, cardiologist and his personal physician, Dr Faisal Sultan. Dr Uzma was also to be included in the board.The court ordered that his medical records remain confidential and barred political activity or media interactions outside the hospital. It also directed authorities to arrange telephone contact between Imran and his children.Justice Waheed stressed that access to family could not be treated as a favour, describing the meetings as a fundamental right rather than a concession. The court, however, required PTI representatives to refrain from political activity or media engagement after meeting Imran, a condition the party said it would follow.Aleema Khan welcomed the order, saying the family had been demanding hospital treatment for Imran for months. Speaking to reporters at the Dahgal checkpoint in Rawalpindi, she said she was happy about the meeting but remained uncertain about whether the development signalled a broader change in circumstances.“"Words cannot describe how happy I am about the meeting. I cannot even imagine where I would have got sweets from. I have appeared before the ATC Rawalpindi from the Supreme Court,” Aleema said.She also rejected suggestions that the family was politicising Imran’s health, saying they were speaking as his sisters.PTI spokesperson Niazullah Khan Niazi said Imran had a right to meet his family twice a week but that authorities had continued to restrict access despite an Islamabad High Court order. He said the party would comply with the Supreme Court’s direction against political statements after meetings.Concerns over Imran’s health have intensified in recent months. A medical report submitted to the Supreme Court said he had experienced fluctuating blood pressure, palpitations, headaches, restlessness and significant anxiety.A PIMS cardiologist who examined him on August 1 recorded his blood pressure at 140/100mmHg and recommended measures to reduce mental stress, including more frequent meetings with his wife and access to reading material. A four-member medical board that examined him on August 10 recorded his blood pressure at 140/80mmHg and recommended walking, relaxation and more frequent interaction with his immediate family and spouse.The report said Imran had undergone at least 39 medical check-ups since his incarceration, with jail medical officers examining him three times a day. It also said his ECG was normal and his vision had improved to almost normal following treatment for an eye condition.PTI has questioned the authenticity and completeness of the medical documentation and demanded examinations by Imran’s personal physicians, Dr Asim Yusuf and Dr Faisal Sultan, as well as an independent medical board. The government has rejected claims that he is being denied proper medical care, saying he is receiving treatment from specialists in accordance with the law and court orders.A report submitted to the Supreme Court in February had said Imran’s right eye was functioning at only 15% capacity. The court subsequently ordered that he be granted access to his personal physicians in Adiala Jail.Imran and Bushra Bibi remain incarcerated at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi. They were sentenced in December 2025 to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case over allegations that they unlawfully retained a Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince.Imran has been in custody since August 2023, initially following his conviction in the £190 million corruption case. He also faces pending trials under Pakistan’s Anti-Terrorism Act in connection with the May 9, 2023, protests.Imran, who served as prime minister from 2018 until his ouster through a parliamentary no-confidence vote in 2022, and his supporters have consistently maintained that the cases against him are politically motivated and aimed at preventing his political comeback.
Article Summary: Imran's sister Noreen Niazi met him at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail on Tuesday after a gap of around nine months. Meeting followed a Supreme Court order allowing weekly meetings between the former prime minister and his family amid concerns over his health.

Article Title: Democrat Angie Nixon defeats Alexander Vindman in surprise Florida Senate primary upset
Article Text:
File photo: Democratic socialist Angie Nixon (right) and former national security official Alexander Vindman

Nixon backed by progressives, faces tough November race

Donalds, Jolly win governor primaries

Redistricting reshapes Florida House races

Democratic socialist Angie Nixon scored a surprise victory in Florida’s Democratic primary for the US Senate on Tuesday, defeating retired Army officer and former national security official Alexander Vindman, according to projections by media outlets cited by Reuters.Nixon, a Florida state legislator since 2020, will now face Republican Senator Ashley Moody in the November general election for the final two years of former Senator Marco Rubio’s term. Rubio left the Senate after becoming US secretary of state under President Donald Trump.The result was a notable upset for Nixon, who was heavily outspent by Vindman and emerged from a primary in which the former Army officer had significant name recognition from his role in Trump’s first impeachment.Vindman testified before Congress in 2019 about a phone call between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. After his defeat, Vindman said on social media, "Rep. Nixon ran a strong campaign. I will be standing by her side in the fight against Ashley Moody. I hope you'll join me."Meanwhile, Trump took a jibe at Vindman and wrote on Truth Social, “SleazeBag Vindman loses tonight to a Radical Left Lunatic.How cool is that???”.Nixon, 42, has been active in Florida’s labour movement and has positioned herself as a progressive candidate. She was backed by prominent progressives, including Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota.She also attracted attention earlier this year after being reprimanded for disrupting a vote in the Florida House while protesting congressional redistricting legislation with a pink megaphone. During her campaign, she urged supporters to "make sure you wear your pink to the polls."If elected, Nixon would become Florida’s first Black US senator.However, the November contest is expected to be difficult for Democrats. Nonpartisan analysts favour Moody, who was appointed to Rubio’s Senate seat by Republican Governor Ron DeSantis after Rubio became secretary of state.Florida has shifted sharply to the right in recent elections. Trump won the state by 13 percentage points in 2024, while Democrats have not elected a US senator from Florida since 2012.The Senate primary was part of a broader set of Florida contests that will determine the state’s political direction in November.Republican Representative Byron Donalds won the Republican nomination for governor, while former Republican Congressman David Jolly won the Democratic nomination, according to the Associated Press.Donalds, who has Trump's backing, would become Florida’s first Black governor if he wins in November. He defeated former Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, political newcomer James Fishback and other Republican contenders."The primary is over," Donalds told supporters after his victory. "Tonight we put aside our differences. Tonight we are one united Republican Party."Jolly switched from the Republican Party to the Democrats last year and has sought to present himself as a centrist candidate.He said his approach would combine elements of both parties, including support for capitalism and limited government alongside greater government involvement in areas such as education and housing.The November election will also test Trump's influence in his adopted home state and Democrats' efforts to make Florida competitive again.Several congressional races were also decided in Tuesday's primaries after Florida adopted new congressional maps designed to strengthen Republican prospects.Democratic Representative Jared Moskowitz was projected to win his primary in the 25th Congressional District and will face Republican Scott Singer in November.Longtime Democratic Representative Debbie Wasserman Schultz also won her party's nomination in a redrawn South Florida district with a plurality-Black electorate.Her candidacy had drawn criticism from activists and Democratic challengers who argued that the historically Black district should be represented by a Black lawmaker.On the Republican side, state Representative Mike Beltran was projected to win the nomination to challenge Democratic Representative Kathy Castor in a district redrawn to favour Republicans.Florida's new map could leave the state with a congressional delegation of 24 Republicans and just four Democrats, according to Reuters.Republican Representative Cory Mills also lost his primary to former television news anchor Ryan Elijah. Mills has denied allegations of campaign-finance violations and sexual misconduct that are being examined by the House Ethics Committee.The results underline the uphill task facing Florida Democrats: while Nixon's upset has given the party an unexpected boost in the Senate race, Republicans remain strongly favoured across much of the state's political landscape heading into November.
Article Summary: Democratic socialist Angie Nixon scored a surprise victory in Florida’s Democratic primary for the US Senate on Tuesday. Nixon, a Florida state legislator since 2020, will now face Republican Senator Ashley Moody in the November general election. The result was a notable upset for Nixon, who was heavily outspent by Vindman.

Article Title: US vs ICC row escalates: Trump administration sanctions international court president, senior lawyer
Article Text:
Trump administration sanctioned ICC president Tomoko Akane

The United States on Tuesday imposed sanctions on International Criminal Court president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, in the latest escalation of the Trump administration’s campaign against the Hague-based court.US secretary of state Marco Rubio said the sanctions were imposed under an executive order signed by President Donald Trump last year. Akane, a Japanese judge, heads the ICC, while Seye, a Senegalese national, is a senior trial lawyer on the prosecution team that sought an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He has also been nominated for election as an ICC judge.“These individuals have directly engaged in efforts by the ICC to investigate, arrest, detain, or prosecute officials whose government has not consented to ICC jurisdiction,” Rubio said, as quoted by Reuters.The ICC condemned the sanctions, saying they threatened the international legal order. “When judicial actors are threatened for applying the law, it is the international legal order itself that is placed at risk,” the court said.The move has also put Washington at odds with European allies. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said the Netherlands, which hosts the ICC, disapproved of the sanctions and had invited Akane to discuss the country’s continued support for the court.“International courts and tribunals must be able to freely carry out their mandates,” Berendsen said.The latest sanctions freeze any US assets held by Akane and Seye and effectively cut them off from the US financial system. The US Treasury also issued a general licence allowing transactions involving the two officials to be wound down through September 17.The United States has never been a member of the ICC and has long opposed its jurisdiction over US officials. The court was established in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity. Under its statute, it can prosecute atrocity crimes committed on the territory of member states even when the accused is a national of a non-member country.The Trump administration has previously sanctioned several ICC prosecutors and judges over the court’s investigations and arrest warrants involving Netanyahu and former Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Gallant, as well as its past investigation into US troops in Afghanistan.Trump has said the campaign is aimed at defending Netanyahu and others from prosecution. Rubio said last month that Washington would step up efforts to undermine the ICC, including by persuading other countries to leave the institution.Akane had warned in December that US sanctions could “rapidly undermine the court’s operations in all situations and cases, and jeopardize its very existence”.
Article Summary: US sanctions International Criminal Court president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye. US secretary of state Marco Rubio said the sanctions were imposed under an executive order signed by President Donald Trump last year. Akane, a Japanese judge, heads the ICC, while Seye is a Senegalese national.

Article Title: “Too r*tarded to k*ll her husband": Candace Owens confronts Andrew Wilson over Charlie Kirk claims after controversial comments about Erika Kirk
Article Text:
Candace Owens and Andrew Wilson clash over Charlie Kirk case

Andrew Wilson’s controversial remark draws attention

tarded to k

Candace Owens and Andrew Wilson turned a heated debate about Charlie Kirk ’s assassination into a broader confrontation over evidence, accountability and the growing divisions inside the American right. Their lengthy exchange on the PBD Podcast drew widespread attention after Wilson made a sweeping insult toward women while defending an earlier social media comment about Kirk’s widow. The exchange quickly moved beyond the original argument, exposing just how bitter the dispute has become.The August 14 discussion centered on the circumstances surrounding Kirk’s fatal shooting and the prosecution of Tyler Robinson. Wilson argued that the available evidence points toward Robinson as the person responsible, citing investigative material including charging documents, DNA evidence, surveillance footage and alleged messages connected to the case.Owens questioned parts of that narrative. Rather than accepting the evidence at face value, she raised concerns about the timeline, security arrangements and the reliability of certain forensic details. Her approach reflected the larger controversy surrounding the case, where competing interpretations have continued to circulate online.At one point, Owens demonstrated that she knew the charges against Robinson in detail.When Wilson suggested she was relying on information from her phone, she gave it to host Patrick Bet-David, apparently to show that she could discuss the case without using it during the exchange.The confrontation became even more personal when Owens brought up one of Wilson’s previous comments concerning Kirk’s widow. She read his own words back to him, prompting an offensive response that became one of the most widely discussed moments from the debate.Owens quoted Wilson’s earlier description of Kirk’s widow as “too rll her husband.” Rather than distancing himself from the language, Wilson expanded his statement during the livestream, saying, “I Just Think All Women Are R*tarded.”The remark immediately changed the tone of the conversation. What had begun as an argument about evidence and the assassination investigation became a highly contentious discussion about Wilson’s treatment of women and his willingness to defend provocative statements in front of a large audience.The dispute also highlights the increasingly fractured nature of conservative media. Owens and Wilson represent different approaches to political commentary, and their disagreement over the Kirk case has become part of a much wider argument about whom audiences should trust when examining controversial events.Kirk was fatally shot on September 10, 2025, during a Turning Point USA event at Utah Valley University in Utah. Robinson, who was 22 at the time, surrendered the following day after his parents recognized him in surveillance images, according to the account provided in the reference material. His criminal case has not yet gone to trial.That distinction remains important. Allegations, courtroom evidence and online theories are not the same thing. Until the case proceeds through the legal system, claims surrounding Robinson’s guilt, the evidence against him and any possible wider involvement should be treated carefully.The Owens-Wilson confrontation nevertheless shows how intensely the case continues to divide commentators. Their three-hour debate was not simply a disagreement over one investigation. It became a spectacle of competing narratives, personal attacks and deep mistrust, all unfolding before a massive online audience.
Article Summary: Candace Owens and Andrew Wilson turned a heated debate about Charlie Kirk ’s assassination into a broader confrontation. Their lengthy exchange drew widespread attention after Wilson made a sweeping insult toward women. The exchange quickly moved beyond the original argument, exposing just how bitter the dispute has become.

Article Title: Is JollyIRL still alive? Kick streamer's major update after frightening bungee jump incident
Article Text:
Is JollyIRL alive? Kick streamer gives update after bungee jump

JollyIRL bungee jump incident sparks reaction from fans and other streamers

Is JollyIRL still alive? The question spread rapidly among viewers after the Kick streamer’s bungee jump livestream in Pattaya, Thailand, ended moments after she made the leap. A sudden cut in the broadcast, followed by a loud scream, left fans with little information and plenty of worry. JollyIRL has since addressed the incident herself, confirming that she survived and explaining that she was dealing with pain after the jump.The concern began when footage from JollyIRL’s livestream circulated online. The clip showed her preparing for the jump before she eventually stepped off the platform. The moment became difficult to interpret once the broadcast abruptly stopped.For viewers watching remotely, there was no immediate explanation. That uncertainty quickly fueled speculation across social media. Some people feared she had suffered a serious accident, while others simply wanted confirmation that she was safe.The situation changed when JollyIRL posted an update on X. She confirmed that she was alive and described the physical discomfort she experienced after the jump."I’m good I’m not dead my arm and neck just hurt I think I got whiplash BUT I see some of the reactions and realize some of yall AINT S***"Her message reassured worried followers, although her reference to possible whiplash also showed why the abrupt end to the livestream had caused concern. Neck pain following a high-impact activity can be uncomfortable and, depending on the circumstances, may require medical attention.The incident also sparked a wider discussion among viewers about the risks involved in livestreamed stunts. What looks like a quick adrenaline-filled moment on screen can carry real physical risks, particularly when a jump involves sudden movement and force.Once JollyIRL confirmed that she was safe, the tone of the online conversation shifted from fear to relief. Fans who had initially worried about the worst outcome began sending messages hoping she would recover quickly.One viewer wrote, "That’s why that shit is bad and dangerous cause you can f*** your neck up permanently..glad you good"Another follower expressed how alarming the situation had been, saying, "Jolly you had us worried sick"The incident also caught the attention of fellow streamer Sneako. While reacting to the circulating footage during his own livestream, he appeared concerned about what had happened and offered a simple message of support."That does not sound good at all. Bro, anyway. I hope she’s okay."His reaction added to the wave of concern surrounding the clip before JollyIRL’s own statement provided clarity.For now, the key update is straightforward: JollyIRL is alive. She reported pain in her neck and arm and said she believed she may have suffered whiplash. Her update put an end to the most alarming speculation, but the episode has also reminded viewers that livestream entertainment does not remove the risks associated with extreme activities.The viral bungee jump clip may have lasted only moments, but its impact continued long after the stream ended. JollyIRL’s confirmation gave her audience the answer it had been waiting for, while the incident highlighted how quickly uncertainty can spread when a livestream suddenly goes silent.
Article Summary: JollyIRL bungee jump incident sparks reaction from fans and other streamers. A sudden cut in the broadcast, followed by a loud scream, left fans with little information and plenty of worry. JollyIRL has since addressed the incident herself, confirming that she survived.

Article Title: IShowSpeed teases a WWE return "very soon" after WrestleMania 42 appearance and explosive Logan Paul rivalry
Article Text:
IShowSpeed (Image Via Instagram)

IShowSpeed hints at WWE return after WrestleMania 42

IShowSpeed and Logan Paul rivalry could continue in WWE

IShowSpeed may not be finished with WWE just yet. The popular streamer has hinted that another run inside the wrestling ring could be coming sooner than fans expect. During a recent livestream, Speed said he plans to return to WWE "very soon," reigniting interest in what could be his next major wrestling appearance. His WrestleMania 42 debut already showed that he can turn a celebrity cameo into a memorable WWE moment.Speed’s latest comment has added fresh fuel to speculation about his future with WWE. While he did not reveal a specific date, his use of "very soon" suggests that fans may not have to wait long before seeing him involved with the company again.The streamer has built a reputation for bringing unpredictable energy to major sporting and entertainment events, and WWE proved to be a natural fit. His WrestleMania 42 appearance in April gave him the chance to step beyond his usual streaming environment and become part of an actual wrestling storyline.Speed joined Logan Paul and Austin Theory for a six-man tag team match against The Usos and LA Knight. Although his team failed to secure the victory, the match did not end Speed’s involvement in the action.Instead, the post-match sequence became one of the most memorable parts of his appearance.After Paul turned against him, Speed eventually got his revenge by driving the WWE star through an announce table. The moment gave the streamer a dramatic payoff and added a personal edge to what could otherwise have been a standard celebrity appearance.That history gives WWE several possible directions if Speed returns.A renewed rivalry with Logan Paul would be an obvious option. Their WrestleMania 42 encounter already established tension between the two personalities, and WWE could easily build on that history if both men remain involved.There is also a larger reason Speed could have another opportunity. WWE has increasingly embraced personalities from outside traditional wrestling, particularly creators and major internet stars who can bring new audiences to its programming.Speed fits that strategy unusually well. His enormous online following, energetic personality and willingness to throw himself into unexpected situations make him an easy choice for a promotion that thrives on spectacle.Still, a future WWE appearance does not necessarily mean Speed is preparing for a full-time wrestling career. His schedule remains centered on streaming and entertainment, so another WWE role could range from a one-night appearance to a larger storyline.For now, his "very soon" comment is the biggest clue available. There is no confirmed return date in the information provided, but the possibility has already given fans something to speculate about.If WWE decides to bring Speed back, the company has plenty of material to work with. His WrestleMania 42 debut created a storyline with Logan Paul, gave viewers a chaotic table spot and established that Speed can hold his own in WWE’s high-energy environment. A second appearance could take that momentum even further.
Article Summary: IShowSpeed said he plans to return to WWE "very soon" during a recent livestream. His WrestleMania 42 appearance in April gave him the chance to step beyond his usual streaming environment and become part of an actual wrestling storyline. There is no confirmed return date in the information provided, but the possibility has given fans something to speculate about.

Article Title: Indian-origin grandmother with Green Card detained by ICE after living in the US for 30 years. Her daughter is an immigration attorney
Article Text:
Venkata Vasamsetty (middle) has been in the US for 30 years and has been a Green Card holder since 2013.

What is Venkata Vasamsetty's story?

Can a Green Card holder be arrested?

Venkata Vasamsetty, who has lived in the US for 30 years and is a Green Card holder, has been detained by ICE in a bizarre case of immigration while her daughter Yashaswini Vasamsetty is an employment-based immigration attorney licensed in Texas and New Jersey. Yashaswini's friend Zoe Ji Wilson shared the ordeal of Venkata Vasamsetty as Vasamsetty's family is collecting signatures for a 'Free Venkata' campaign.Venkata has been in the US legally for 30 years and she got her Green Card in 2013. She is a teacher with the Wake County Public School System in North Carolina, owns a house and is the mother to two daughters, who are US citizens. She is also a grandmother to US citizens. The family said that Venkata does not have any criminal records and not even a speeding ticket ever.Yes, a Green Card holder can be arrested if they break the conditions that one needs to fulfil as a Green Card holder. An absence of more than six months from the US can raise questions about whether a permanent resident intended to abandon their US residence. This happened in Vasamsetty's case during a Covid emergency.In July 2022, Venkata traveled to India to see her father, who was suffering from several medical conditions.She got COVID in November and had to defer her return to the US as she had to be hospitalized in India for nearly two weeks. She returned to the US in February 2023 -- after spending seven months outside the US.She was stopped at the Raleigh-Durham International Airport as she returned and the DHS told her that she had been abroad for a long period, which made a case of intention to abandon the Green Card. But she was, at that time, in the process of purchasing a house in North Carolina and had no intention of going back to India.ICE gave her a date to appear in immigration court and allowed her to go home to her family for the time being. She was asked to report to ICE’s Charlotte office on a regular basis. Her family said that Venkata attended every single ICE appointment and they submitted all the documents to prove that it was only the situation that delayed her and she had no intention to leave the US.A court then finally ordered in favour of Venkata and said that the DHS could not meet their "burden of proving by clear and convincing evidence" that Vasamsetty was removable as charged.On May 19, 2026, the case against Vasamsetty was terminated and she was moved out of the removal proceedings. But she had a scheduled ICE appointment on July 11. ICE did not cancel the date and Vasamsetty did not skip the appointment either assuming that she did not have any need to appear as the case ws dropped. She took the court order to the appointment but she was asked to come a month later as ICE did not have its records updated. When she went for the August 11 appointment, she was detained.Vasamsetty was taken to Irwin County Detention Center in Ocilla, Georgia."No warning. No notice. No opportunity to prepare. No regard for the fact that an Immigration Judge had already terminated her removal proceedings. No regard for the fact that she is severely diabetic and did not have her insulin, medications, or medical supplies with her. No regard for any of that. They put her in handcuffs and took her into custody. DHS did not file a new Notice to Appear until the day after she was detained. She was not in proceedings at the time of her arrest," Wilson wrote in her post."If this can happen to Yesh's mother, people need to understand what this means. It means lawful status, decades of compliance, a clean record, a court order, and even basic medical vulnerability may still not be enough to protect someone from being detained and stripped of their freedom. That should terrify all of us," Wilson wrote noting that not everyone has lawyers in their families.
Article Summary: Venkata Vasamsetty has been in the US legally for 30 years and she got her Green Card in 2013. She is a teacher with the Wake County Public School System in North Carolina, owns a house and is the mother to two daughters, who are US citizens. The family said that Venkata does not have any criminal records and not even a speeding ticket ever.

Article Title: A Costa Rican mother saved for 9 years to buy land, then built her home with 7 tonnes of recycled plastic
Article Text:
Cindy Mora and her son's home used about 850 blocks made from recycled plastic, PC: Econews

How recycled plastic was turned into the home's walls

Why the claim that 800 volunteers built the house is misleading

What the plastic-block home was designed to demonstrate

Cindy Mora Abarca spent 9 years saving money for a small plot of land in the Lámparas neighbourhood of Alajuelita, near San José, Costa Rica, hoping to eventually build a permanent home for herself and her 6-year-old son, Fabrizio. She eventually secured the land through a loan, but that left her without enough money to construct a house on it. Her situation changed when she connected with Habitat for Humanity Costa Rica, which paired her case with Procter & Gamble, the local organisation Urbarium and recycled materials group Ekojunto. Together, the partners built a home using interlocking blocks made primarily from recycled plastic waste, giving Mora and her son a permanent place to live. Construction began in April 2018, and the completed house was handed over to the family on May 26 that year. The project turned thousands of kilograms of discarded plastic into the walls of a real family home, while also demonstrating how recycled materials could be incorporated into conventional residential construction.According to reporting by La Nación, the house used approximately 7 tons of recycled plastic, with the material supplied through Procter & Gamble's corporate social responsibility programme.The plastic was processed into interlocking construction units known as Bloqueplas, a system developed to allow the pieces to fit together much like Lego blocks. Andrea Ramírez of Urbarium described the construction method as a practical way to transform plastic waste into building material rather than simply sending it for disposal. Recent retellings of the project commonly cite around 850 blocks, although the original Costa Rican reporting primarily emphasised the roughly 7 tons of recycled plastic used in the construction. The plastic blocks formed the home's walls, while conventional materials and methods were still used for the foundation, roof, plumbing, electrical wiring, doors and windows. Once the structure was completed and finished with plaster and paint, the house looked much like any other modest home in the surrounding neighbourhood rather than resembling an experimental recycling project.One detail that has repeatedly become distorted as the story has resurfaced online is the claim that 800 volunteers built the home. The original reporting describes more than 800 combined hours of volunteer labour, primarily contributed by Procter & Gamble employees, rather than 800 individual people working on the house. That distinction is important because the two figures describe completely different scales of participation. Habitat for Humanity Costa Rica was involved in selecting Mora's family based on socioeconomic need and ensuring that the property met the necessary requirements for construction, while Urbarium coordinated the local implementation of the recycled plastic block system. Volunteers then contributed their labour during the construction process, working alongside the organisations involved in the project. The home was therefore the result of a partnership between a housing organisation, a private company, local specialists and volunteers, rather than hundreds of people independently coming together to construct a house from plastic.The project was presented as an example of how plastic waste could be diverted into a useful, durable construction material while helping provide affordable housing. Urbarium publicly attributed several additional properties to its block system, including resistance to seismic forces, thermal and acoustic insulation and protection against weather. Those claims, however, should be treated as claims made by the organisation involved in the project, rather than independently verified characteristics of Mora's specific house; no independent testing specific to the home has been identified. The blocks were also designed to comply with Costa Rica's 2010 seismic construction code, according to project materials. For Mora, however, the environmental experiment was secondary to the practical outcome. After spending years saving for land and then struggling to afford construction, she finally had a permanent home where she could raise her son. The project became an early documented example in Costa Rica of recycled plastic being incorporated into a functioning residential building, showing that discarded material could become part of a home's physical structure rather than simply being treated as waste.
Article Summary: Cindy Mora Abarca and her son's home used about 850 blocks made from recycled plastic. The house used approximately 7 tons of recycled plastic, with the material supplied through Procter & Gamble's corporate social responsibility programme. The project was presented as an example of how plastic waste could be diverted into a useful, durable construction material while helping provide affordable housing.

Article Title: California startup JetZero is building a $3 billion 'manta ray' aircraft that promises to cut fuel consumption by 50%, carry 250 passengers and replace traditional windows with screens; Japan Airlines
Article Text:
A 'manta ray' shaped aircraft

The fuel claim that has everyone hooked

A long-existing concept

Japan Airlines on board

A California-based startup, JetZero, is all set to move closer to a real-world test of a 'manta ray' aircraft that could change the future of the airline industry forever. According to the startup, its planned Z4 will carry about 250 passengers, fly roughly 5,750 miles and use 30% to 50% less fuel than the aircraft in service today. The company presented the project during the Farnborough International Airshow, held in the United Kingdom from July 20 to July 24, 2026. Japan Airlines has now joined the program to provide operational input.The company aims to have a full-scale prototype airborne by 2027 and hopes to launch commercial operations in the early 2030s. In July, JetZero announced a $3 billion deal with the U.S. government to finance a factory in North Carolina aimed at accelerating the development and future production of the aircraft.The major innovation of the aircraft lies in its very shape. Most commercial jets use a "tube and wing" layout, with passengers inside a cylindrical fuselage while two separate wings produce most of the lift that keeps the aircraft in the air. The Z4 uses a blended-wing-body configuration. Its wide, flattened centre section flows gradually into the wings, allowing much more of the structure to generate lift and creating a smoother path for air around the aircraft.Less aerodynamic drag means the engines need less energy to push the plane forward.Jet fuel is a major operating expense, and the reduction of 50% would affect both environmental performance and the cost of flying each seat. For the most part, burning less conventional aviation fuel also means producing less carbon dioxide per trip.Still, the number is a company target, not a result from a certified passenger aircraft. Even if the Z4 reaches it, the plane would not be emission-free, and the final savings would depend on route length, payload, weather, engine choice, and how airlines configure and operate it.The project envisions a maximum range of approximately 5,000 nautical miles, roughly equivalent to 9,200 kilometres. As a point of reference, this distance is sufficient to cover the route between São Paulo and Madrid, which is estimated at about 8,400 kilometres.About 250 passengers would be distributed across six sections of the cabin, with each seat having access to its own luggage compartment. However, traditional side windows are not part of the design. Instead, screens connected to high-definition cameras will display external images during flight, while two skylights near the front rows will allow natural light to enter. The proposed capacity also fills an awkward space in today’s market. With about 250 seats, the aircraft would sit between the largest single-aisle jets and the bigger twin-aisle models used on many long-haul routes. Its projected range could cover a large share of medium- and long-distance services without forcing airlines into a much larger aircraft.The basic idea has been studied for decades. A Boeing, NASA, and U.S. Air Force team flew the remotely piloted X-48B and X-48C demonstrators more than 100 times, examining low-speed stability, takeoffs, landings, and flight-control behaviour. The tests showed that an unusual, tailless aircraft could be controlled through demanding parts of a flight.Airbus followed another route with MAVERIC, a small remote-controlled demonstrator that first flew in June 2019. The manufacturer estimated that its blended-wing-body configuration could reduce fuel consumption by as much as 20% compared with a current single-aisle aircraft using the same engine.Those projects helped engineers understand the shape, but neither became a commercial passenger jet. JetZero is trying to cross that gap. That is the big difference. But before passengers can board a Z4, the company must prove that the architecture works at full scale. Scaled Composites, a Northrop Grumman subsidiary, is building the Jet1 demonstrator which is scheduled to make its first flight in 2027.The U.S. Department of the Air Force backs the project, selecting the developer for a $235 million blended-wing-body prototype effort. The military sees potential for lower fuel demand, longer range, and more efficient cargo movement, while the same testing could provide useful evidence for a future civilian aircraft.The Z4 has already attracted the attention of some of the largest airlines in the United States. JetZero has agreements with industry companies, and United Airlines plans to purchase up to 200 units of the aircraft. Delta and Alaska Airlines are also among the companies supporting the development of the new platform.The developer says it is designing the Z4 to use existing airport infrastructure without specialised or costly changes, a crucial point for airlines that cannot rebuild terminals, taxi routes, and ground equipment around one new model.Japan Airlines will bring its expertise in flight operations, cabin service, maintenance and ground handling to the partnership. The two companies will also study gate management and a future maintenance, repair and overhaul system to support operators after the aircraft enters service. Japan Airlines executive officer for corporate strategy Takao Suzuki said the partnership supports the airline’s commitment to “sustainable innovation and net-zero emissions by 2050”. JetZero CEO and co-founder Tom O’Leary said the planned launch in the early 2030s fits the airline’s longer-term plans.
Article Summary: California-based startup, JetZero, is all set to move closer to a real-world test of a'manta ray' aircraft. According to the startup, its planned Z4 will carry about 250 passengers, fly roughly 5,750 miles and use 30% to 50% less fuel than aircraft in service today. Japan Airlines has now joined the program to provide operational input.

Article Title: Ex-Cambridge scholar Nathan Cofnas who exposed Jason Arday plagiarism claims says he could be murdered after thousands rally at Trafalgar Square
Article Text:
Nathan Cofnas (left), Jason Arday (right)

Cofnas says Trafalgar Square gathering made him fear for his life

Cofnas published side-by-side comparisons from Arday’s thesis

Earlier reviews and investigations also examined his academic work

Questions spread to Arday’s professional biography

Cambridge announced an investigation before his resignation

Arday was found dead days after resigning

Former Cambridge academic Nathan Cofnas says he fears for his safety in London after thousands gathered at Trafalgar Square on Monday for a vigil honouring former Cambridge professor Jason Arday. Arday, 41, died days after resigning from the university amid allegations of plagiarism and questions about his academic career. Cofnas brought the controversy into the public spotlight in July after revealing extensive similarities between passages in Arday’s 2015 PhD thesis and earlier academic work. The Guardian later independently identified more than 100 passages with similarities. Arday also faced scrutiny over claims concerning academic positions, fundraising, athletic achievements and other details in his professional biography. Cambridge announced an investigation into his qualifications, honorary appointments and academic-misconduct complaints on August 5, the same day he resigned.Cofnas made the claim on X as the August 17 vigil was taking place. He described the gathering as an “anti-Cofnas hate rally” and said that, had he been in London, he believed there was a real possibility he could have been murdered. Speakers at the event criticised people who had questioned Arday's academic record, with Cofnas among those singled out.Organisers presented the gathering as a vigil to honour Arday, while attendance estimates put the crowd at about 30,000. There is no established evidence that the wider crowd posed a threat to Cofnas or that anyone at the event attempted to harm him.Cofnas's investigation centred on Arday's 2015 doctoral thesis. He said he used Copyleaks to identify textual similarities with earlier academic work and published side-by-side comparisons of passages. One prominent example involved a 2009 doctoral dissertation by Paula Zwozdiak-Myers, a reader in education at Brunel University London. Cofnas argued that sections of Arday's thesis reproduced wording and ideas from the earlier dissertation with limited changes. He also pointed to passages where, according to his analysis, errors in the earlier material appeared to have been retained. Retraction Watch later reported that dozens of passages identified by Cofnas closely matched Zwozdiak-Myers' dissertation.The allegations did not begin with Cofnas's July analysis. Retraction Watch reported that Times Higher Education had previously prepared a 63-page dossier examining alleged plagiarism in Arday's thesis and journal articles. The report included claims involving material that allegedly appeared inside quotations attributed to people Arday said he had interviewed. Liverpool John Moores University, where Arday completed his PhD, had previously reviewed concerns and did not find plagiarism. Arday denied plagiarism, while acknowledging mistakes in his academic work. The competing claims and findings remain central to the controversy.The scrutiny later expanded beyond his academic writing. The Guardian examined claims about positions and affiliations listed in Arday's professional biography, including references involving Ohio State University, the University of Glasgow and Birkbeck. The newspaper reported that some institutions disputed or could not substantiate certain claims. Questions were also raised about descriptions of his sporting achievements, charity fundraising and other aspects of his public profile. These inquiries broadened the controversy from the contents of his academic work to the accuracy of claims associated with his career.Cambridge announced on August 5 that it was investigating concerns surrounding Arday's qualifications, honorary appointments and academic-misconduct complaints. Arday resigned from the university on the same day, saying the level of scrutiny had become unbearable. The university had previously defended him amid earlier concerns, while the renewed allegations prompted a fresh examination of his credentials and academic record.Arday was found dead at a property in Battersea, south London, on August 13, eight days after his resignation. He was 41. The Metropolitan Police said his death was unexpected but was not being treated as suspicious. His death subsequently prompted the Trafalgar Square vigil on August 17, where thousands gathered to remember him and speakers addressed the controversy surrounding his career.
Article Summary: Former Cambridge academic Nathan Cofnas says he fears for his safety in London. Thousands gathered at Trafalgar Square on Monday for a vigil honouring former Cambridge professor Jason Arday. Arday, 41, died days after resigning from the university amid allegations of plagiarism and questions about his academic career. Cambridge announced an investigation into his qualifications, honorary appointments and academic-misconduct complaints on August 5.

Article Title: 'I don't have courage to take another loan': Indian student in Canada says going back home seems easier, sets up fundraiser
Article Text:
Indian student in Canada Samir Garhwal sets up a fundraiser to pay off his education loans as he was denied a work permit after completing his degree from Portage College.

Row over Portage College degrees

Samir Garhwal, an Indian student who got his degree from Canada's controversial Portage College, said he is in a worse situation now after completing his course than he was two years ago when he came to a new country with an education loan to repay. As thousands of Portage College students were denied work permits in Canada, they have two options left in front of them: going back to India or legally challenging the IRCC's decision to deny them work permits.In an interview with CityNews, Samir said he and his peers were relaxed after their course and were waiting for their work permits to come so that they could start working in Canada and gain Canadian experience. But there was a mass rejection of work permits, leading to the students protesting against the college and Canadian immigration. But as of now, there has been no solution.Canada identified some courses as eligible for a work permit and some as ineligible. There was a change of rule in 2024 that made many courses of this particular college ineligible, but these students enroled in the courses before that date in 2024 and were in the dark about their future in Canada for the last two years."I already took an education loan in India, and in my current situation, I am not willing to or don't have the courage to get another loan," Garhwal, who said he was working while studying in Canada, confessed.For Garhwal and many others, going back to India is the only plausible option as the legal option involves more money. Garhwal has set up a fundraiser to pay his education loan. "Three years ago, I moved to Canada with the hope of building a better future through education and hard work. I have worked toward my studies while managing the challenges of living in a new country, including tuition, living expenses, and other essential costs," Garhwal wrote in the fundraiser.Portage College said they were still seeking clarification on the denial of the work permits for its students. “We are continuing to seek clarification on the Post Graduation Work Permit issue. As each day goes by, we understand the uncertainty that grows for many of our affected graduates as we endeavour to clarify factual and sourced details. We remain committed to informing the public about new developments to the issue,” said Portage College Vice President Academics and Research Dr Donna Feledichuk. “We also encourage affected graduates to seek professional advice from certified immigration specialists.”Juno News reported that the Canadian Institute of Osteopathic Therapy (CIOT) in Calgary, the private college that partnered with Portage College, has two directors tied to a Punjabi recruitment firm whose director was arrested in India during a 2013 police investigation into alleged student immigration fraud.
Article Summary: Thousands of Portage College students were denied work permits in Canada. They have two options left in front of them: going back to India or legally challenging the IRCC's decision to deny them work permits. Samir Garhwal, an Indian student who got his degree from Canada's controversial college, said he is in a worse situation now after completing his course.

Article Title: 'Move Imran Khan to hospital': Pakistan Supreme Court directs govt amid ex-PM's health concerns
Article Text:
Pakistan SC orders Imran Khan’s hospital transfer. photo credit: AP

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe Imran Khan should receive immediate medical attention? Yes, he needs immediate care No, he can stay in jail Unsure, need more information 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan’s Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the government to move imprisoned former prime minister Imran Khan to a hospital, meeting a longstanding demand from his party and family amid growing concerns over his health.Khan, 73, has been in jail since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases that he and his supporters have described as politically motivated. His Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party welcomed the court order, saying it should have come earlier.“It’s a very welcome order and we wish it had happened sooner so his eye and general health would not have deteriorated this much,” PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari told Reuters.“He should remain in hospital until all doctors are satisfied,” Bukhari added.According to Khan’s spokesperson Naeem Haider Panjutha, the court directed that he be moved to Shifa International Hospital within 48 hours and remain there until September 16.Also Read: 'Needs to be moved to hospital now': Imran Khan's health in jail deteriorates The order came amid renewed concerns over Khan’s physical and mental health. His sons, Sulaiman Khan and Kasim Khan, have repeatedly raised concerns about his access to family, lawyers and doctors.“We have no updates because his family, doctors and lawyers haven’t been allowed to see him for seven months,” they told CNN earlier this month.The development came after former Pakistani president Arif Alvi also said on Tuesday that Khan’s medical reports were “alarming”, citing concerns over anxiety, palpitations and high blood pressure.In a post on X, Alvi said, “Imran Khan’s medical reports are alarming. I have gone through them with several specialists, and I am writing this in plain language so every Pakistani can understand exactly what is happening.”Alvi said the issues that concerned him most were Khan’s “anxiety and stress levels”, “palpitations,” and “high blood pressure”.Alvi also raised concerns over Khan’s heart rate and called for further medical monitoring, including a 24-hour Holter monitor.“I am deeply worried. Isolation is taking a physical toll on his body. If this is not addressed immediately, the damage may become irreversible with more complications to follow,” Alvi said.Calling for Khan to be hospitalised, the former president said: “@ImranKhanPTI definitely needs to be moved to a hospital environment now, under an independent panel of doctors.”Khan’s legal troubles intensified after his ouster as prime minister in a no-confidence vote in 2022. He has faced multiple cases, including those involving state gifts and an unlawful marriage, with some convictions suspended or overturned and appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing.The PTI, which came to power in 2018 and retains a significant support base, was stripped of its election symbol before the 2024 general election, forcing its candidates to contest as independents.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court orders former prime minister Imran Khan to be moved to a hospital. Khan has been in jail since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases. His party welcomed the court order, saying it should have come earlier. The order came amid renewed concerns over Khan’s physical and mental health.

Article Title: Trump claims '24,000 noncitizens voted in 2020 election', urges Congress to pass SAVE America Act
Article Text:
Trump claims 24,000 noncitizens voted in 2020 election

US President Donald Trump has claimed that more than 24,000 noncitizens voted illegally in the 2020 US presidential election, citing what he said was an ongoing review of voter and citizenship records by the US Census Bureau.In a post on X, Trump said the bureau had begun checking voter records from the 2020 election against citizenship records. He claimed the initial review covered 128 million voters and alleged that the exercise had already identified more than 24,000 noncitizens who voted illegally.Trump also said the review of another 32 million voters would produce a much larger number of cases, while renewing his call for Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, which seeks stricter citizenship and identification requirements for federal elections.Trump said, "The US Census Bureau has begun checking the Voter Records from 2020 against their Citizenship Records. On the first 128,000,000 Voters, the Census Bureau proves that over 24,000 Noncitizens voted illegally! The Census Bureau is going to analyze the next 32,000,000 Voters, and this number will explode. I WON THE ELECTION! We must pass THE SAVE AMERICA ACT. Thank you for your attention to this matter."The claim comes a day after Trump cited India's election system while pressing lawmakers to support the proposed legislation.He had pointed to India's use of voter identification and its limited reliance on postal voting as an example of what he described as stronger safeguards.Trump has repeatedly urged Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, arguing that federal elections should be restricted to US citizens and that voters should be required to provide identification and proof of citizenship.The White House has described the proposed legislation as a measure to ensure that only US citizens are eligible to vote in federal elections. It has also called for states to remove noncitizens from federal voter rolls.The bill was introduced in Congress on January 29. According to the background provided by the White House, it would require proof of US citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections and mandate valid identification.The proposed legislation would also restrict mail-in voting, with exceptions for circumstances including illness, disability, military service and travel.Trump's latest post links his election-related claims directly to the legislation, arguing that an alleged presence of noncitizens on voter rolls and among voters demonstrates the need for stricter voting rules.Trump had earlier highlighted India's electoral system while making his case for the legislation.In a post on Truth Social, he referred to a conversation involving Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and said, "Earlier this month, India’s Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, asked our Administration, How can you have Elections in the US without a valid Photo ID?"Referring to India's last general election, Trump said, "India's last Election had 646,000,000 Voters! Less than 1 per cent voted by mail, and every single Voter had to have a VALID Photo Identity Document."Trump subsequently called for Congress to act on the proposed legislation, saying, "We need to pass THE SAVE AMERICA ACT, now!"The White House has also compared US election procedures with those in other countries, arguing that India and Brazil tie voter identification to biometric databases, while the US largely relies on self-attestation for citizenship.The SAVE America Act is aimed at tightening voting rules for federal elections. Its proposed provisions include requiring voters to provide valid identification and proof of US citizenship when registering.It would also require states to remove noncitizens from federal voter rolls and place restrictions on mail-in voting, while allowing exceptions for specific circumstances.Trump has sought support from both Republicans and Democrats for the legislation, arguing that only US citizens should determine the outcome of US elections.His latest claim about the 2020 election comes as he continues to challenge the integrity of the voting process and maintain that he won the election.The claim that more than 24,000 noncitizens voted illegally was made by Trump in his post. The material provided for this story does not independently establish the methodology or findings of the alleged Census Bureau review.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has claimed that more than 24,000 noncitizens voted illegally in the 2020 US presidential election. In a post on X, Trump said the bureau had begun checking voter records from the 2020 election against citizenship records. He claimed the initial review covered 128 million voters and alleged that the exercise had already identified more than 25,000 people who voted illegally. Trump also said the review of another 32 million voters would produce a much larger number of cases.

Article Title: 'They knew': US states accuse Meta of hiding Instagram's impact on teenagers
Article Text: Lawyers representing 29 US states on Tuesday accused Meta of hiding internal research that allegedly found Instagram could be addictive for teenagers, The Guardian reported.The allegations were made as a major legal battle against Meta began in a federal court in Oakland, California. The trial is expected to continue for six to eight weeks.According to the lawsuit, Meta of deliberately designing Instagram and Facebook features to keep young users engaged, despite knowing that some of those features could harm their mental health.Megan O’Neill, a deputy attorney general for California, told the jury that Meta failed to act despite being aware of the risks.“I heard from many of you at jury selection that the health and wellbeing of kids is a shared responsibility,” O’Neill said. “Meta didn’t do its share.”O’Neill said lawyers would present internal documents and testimony obtained during investigations into Meta.She referred to one document that stated, “the young ones are the best ones”. Another allegedly stated: “Teens are hooked despite how it makes them feel. Instagram is addictive.”“They knew,” O’Neill said. “Time and again, profits won.”The 233-page lawsuit, filed in October 2023, also alleges that Meta collected data from children under 13 without parental permission, violating federal and state laws.The states claim Meta “refuses to abandon its use of known harmful features” and has sought to “maximize its financial gains”.The states have said Meta could face damages of up to $200 billion if found liable. They are also seeking changes to Meta's products to make them safer for children.Meta has denied the allegations. Its lawyer, Paul Schmidt, argued that the internal documents and emails presented by the states were selectively quoted and taken out of context.
Article Summary: Lawyers representing 29 US states accused Meta of hiding internal research that allegedly found Instagram could be addictive for teenagers. The allegations were made as a major legal battle against Meta began in a federal court in Oakland, California. The states have said Meta could face damages of up to $200 billion if found liable.

Article Title: In 1969, the US released a European weevil to control invasive thistles; it later fed on more than 30 native species, including at least seven rare or endangered plants
Article Text:
Thistle Head Weevil

thistle head-feeding weevil

Rhinocyllus conicus

Thistle weevil introduction timeline

Agricultural mandate turns into ecological threat

Weevil impact breakdown

Destruction of seed production in rare plants

Policy revisions and modern biological control standards

A European beetle released across North America in 1969 to control invasive pasture weeds became an ecological problem after expanding its diet to more than 30 native plant species, including at least seven rare or threatened thistles. The) was introduced by wildlife and agricultural authorities as a biological control agent against musk thistle (Carduus nutans), an aggressive Eurasian weed that damages livestock rangelands. Instead of staying focused on its target plant, the insect established breeding populations on native North American plants, causing ecological damage across western nature reserves. According to botanical records from the US Department of Agriculture Forest Service Fire Effects Information System (FEIS), Rhinocyllus conicus larvae feed inside flower heads and consume developing seeds before they can spread. Research archived by the University of Maryland Digital Repository shows that this feeding can sharply reduce seed production in native Cirsium thistles, threatening species such as Pitcher's thistle (Cirsium pitcheri) and Platt's thistle (Cirsium xcanescens).1969: R. conicus released in the US to target invasive musk thistle1970s to 1980s: Weevil released across western states and Canada to protect rangelands1990s: Studies confirm feeding on more than 30 native speciesPresent: Federal releases halted, but native plants remain under pressureMusk thistle was accidentally introduced to North America in the late 19th century. It quickly spread through pastures, roadsides, and open fields, reducing available livestock forage. To reduce the need for chemical herbicides, federal researchers approved the import of Rhinocyllus conicus from southern Europe after early laboratory tests examined which plants it could attack. Between 1969 and the mid-1980s, state agencies and university extension services released millions of weevils across agricultural areas in the US and Canada. The insect established self-sustaining populations quickly. Its ability to fly long distances also allowed it to spread beyond farmland into national parks and wildlife refuges.The intended target was musk thistle (Carduus nutans), but the weevil eventually began feeding on more than 30 native Cirsium species. Among the affected plants were C. pitcheri, C. ownbeyi, and C. hydrophilum. The main damage comes from larvae consuming developing seeds inside flower heads, reducing the plants' ability to reproduce. The insect has also spread across large areas of the US Midwest, Great Plains, and Rocky Mountains.Field studies archived by the University of Maryland show that female weevils lay eggs on the bracts of young flower heads. After hatching, the larvae enter the flower head and eat developing ovules, reducing seed production by as much as 80 percent in affected plants. Many native North American thistles depend heavily on seeds to reproduce. Heavy feeding by Rhinocyllus conicus therefore placed additional pressure on small and isolated plant populations. Pitcher's thistle (Cirsium pitcheri) is a federally listed threatened plant found mainly in sand dune habitats around the Great Lakes. Hydrophilus thistle (Cirsium hydrophilum) is an endangered wetland plant native to California marshes. Ownbey's thistle (Cirsium ownbeyi) is a rare species found in rocky canyons across parts of Wyoming, Utah, and Colorado.1969: Initial USDA release of Rhinocyllus conicus in North America1978: Weevils observed feeding on non-target native Cirsium species1996: Major studies document severe seed reduction in native thistles2000s: USDA-APHIS removes R. conicus from approved biological control permitsThe spread of Rhinocyllus conicus to non-target plants helped change federal rules governing biological control programs in North America. The US Department of Agriculture's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (USDA-APHIS) eventually revoked permits for interstate movement of the weevil, ending official release programs. However, stopping new releases did not remove the insect from the environment. Established populations of Rhinocyllus conicus continue to survive in the wild, putting ongoing pressure on native thistles across North America.
Article Summary: Rhinocyllus conicus was released across North America in 1969 as a biological control agent against musk thistle (Carduus nutans) The weevil began feeding on more than 30 native plant species, including at least seven rare or threatened thistles. The main damage comes from larvae consuming developing seeds inside flower heads, reducing the plants' ability to reproduce.

Article Title: Man claims mother-in-law's US visa got 'revoked midflight' for 2-day overstay on previous visit, was sent back from Singapore
Article Text:
Redditor claims that his mother-in-law's US visa was revoked midflight because she was allowed to travel to Singapore from Bengaluru but was barred from boarding the Singapore-Seattle flight. (AI image)

A Redditor shared a strange situation, claiming that his 82-year-old mother-in-law was not allowed to travel from Singapore to Seattle and was told that her visa was revoked. Without explanation, she was told she could not travel any further, and the other family members traveling with her had to return to India to drop her off. The man said that it was a regular 10-year visitor visa which was issued three years ago. The woman traveled to the US on a similar visitor's visa for 20 years and went to the US on this particular visa before.The family reached Singapore from Bengaluru and they were not informed about the visa revocation at the airport.The Reddit post led to confusion as many users claimed that they had never heard of such a situation where a visa got revoked mid-flight. The Redditor later clarified that he found that his mother-in-law overstayed for two days during her previous visit. She had landed in the US on February 22 and was supposed to leave on August 21, but she left on August 23.The man said that the two-day overstay could not be a legitimate justification for not informing them about the visa status."Yes. We have broken the law technically. But not in spirit. And we are ready to pay the consequences for that (visa revocation).A warning instead of revocation would have been kind and generous. But i understand that is not the world we live in. But that doesn't mean they are justified to put us through what they made us go through. Its negligence and harassment. We had to spend thousands of dollars to rebook all tickets, book hotel, etc. And that's just the financial cost," the Redditor said.Social media users said that the visa was not revoked midflight and it must have ben canceled earlier but the authorities in Bengaluru airport did not properly check and let the mother-in-law travel to Singapore.
Article Summary: Redditor claims his 82-year-old mother-in-law's US visa was revoked midflight. She was allowed to travel to Singapore from Bengaluru but was barred from boarding the Singapore-Seattle flight. The man said that it was a regular 10-year visitor visa which was issued three years ago.

Article Title: Pentagon UFO scientist Dr Eric Davis claims US has evidence of 4 alien species after 30 years of UAP research: ‘I’ve seen the evidence, I’ve seen the records’
Article Text:
After 30 years investigating UAPs, Dr Eric Davis says he has seen evidence of alleged extraterrestrial bodies.

Eric Davis claims to have seen evidence of four alien species

Dr Eric Davis claims classified US records document four alleged alien species recovered from crashed UAPs.

Davis says alleged alien bodies were recovered from crashed UFOs

Davis claims records remain classified for decades

Scientist asks Trump for immunity to reveal alleged UFO evidence

Pentagon has not confirmed existence of alien bodies

Other researchers have made similar claims

Dr Eric Davis, an astrophysicist who has worked as a consultant on US government UFO programmes, has claimed that he has seen classified photographs and records that he believes document the recovery of bodies belonging to at least four different alleged extraterrestrial species.Speaking to NewsNation’s Katie Pavlich, Davis claimed the material he had viewed was connected to crashed unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) and that some of the alleged bodies were being kept at highly classified facilities.However, Davis’ claims have not been independently verified, and the US government and military have repeatedly said there is no confirmed physical evidence that extraterrestrial life exists or that alien spacecraft have been recovered.Davis said the material he allegedly reviewed documented at least four different types of beings, which he identified as the Grays, Nordics, Insectoids and Reptilians.“There’s a minimum of four that we know of. I’ve seen the evidence, I’ve seen the records,” Davis said.He described the Grays as resembling the fictional extraterrestrials depicted in Close Encounters of the Third Kind, with small bodies, grey skin, large heads and dark eyes.The alleged Nordics, meanwhile, were described as extremely tall, blonde and Scandinavian-looking, with features that Davis said were the most human-like among the purported species.The other two groups he mentioned were insectoid beings resembling human-sized praying mantises and humanoid creatures with reptilian or lizard-like characteristics.Davis claimed that the photographs, reports and military records he saw involved alleged incidents in which dead bodies were recovered from crashed UFOs.“I don’t know what they eat.
